clue.text: Man and woman on stage

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a step is a stage along the way in a process
hen is informal for a woman, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A couple appear together in a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a man's first name, so a man can be called by it.

clue.text: Fish straying at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fish wanders off into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Abuse old pilot's licence

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: licence means freedom, so the pilot's letters are taken liberties with

parts.note: the fodder is the word pilot, the 's joining it to its licence

explanation.surface: A former airman misuses his flying permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licence' looks like a permit, but it is freedom to rearrange the letters of PILOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to abuse them for your own advantage.

clue.text: Some courses have these weaknesses in theory

definitions.meaning: golf courses are laid out as a series of greens with cups
flaws in an argument, as when one picks gaps in a theory

explanation.surface: Some lessons have flaws in their theoretical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests education, but it is golf courses, which have 9 or 18 of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is played over holes, and a flaw in an argument is a hole in it.

clue.text: Presumably a bottle party that's never going to happen

parts.note: a bottle party would admit bottles but no tins
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A bring-a-bottle party that is never going to take place.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle party, where guests bring bottles, is by implication one with no cans.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a casual refusal meaning it cannot or will not be done.

clue.text: Flogging witch that's eaten wife and family

indicators.note: the witch has swallowed the other pieces, so they sit inside her

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
kin means family or relations

explanation.surface: A witch who has devoured a man's wife and children is being whipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' suggests whipping, but it is used in its slang sense of selling, like a street hawker crying wares.
explanation.definitionFit: Flogging is British slang for selling, and hawking is selling goods by calling out in the street.

clue.text: Perhaps writing in this man's play is no longer relevant

parts.note: his means belonging to this man

indicators.note: the writing letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
writing is one of the three Rs of education, so it gives R

explanation.surface: Perhaps the script of this man's drama is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, hence 'Perhaps writing' for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is history means it is over and done with, of no current importance.

clue.text: He's fallen and knocked Roger down

indicators.note: knocked about means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has tumbled and knocked Roger to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer is a sinner, one fallen from virtue in the moral sense.

clue.text: Quarantine one individual catching athlete's foot on vacation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the individual word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: sole means single or individual

indicators.note: vacated, emptied of everything but its outside letters

explanation.surface: Keep apart a lone person who has picked up a fungal infection while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'athlete's foot' to its outer letters A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to keep them apart from others, which is what quarantine does.

clue.text: Ugly photograph displays architectural feature

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unflattering photo shows a detail of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a glyph is an ornamental vertical groove, as on a Doric frieze.

clue.text: Press broadcast lie about politician

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the politician
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of lie are spread into a new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The newspapers spread a falsehood about a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as the newspapers, but it is a verb, to urge; 'broadcast' rearranges lie to IEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone to act is to urge or drive them on, a synonym of impel.

clue.text: Way of working with journal contributed to intimate, universally relevant study?

indicators.note: the first pieces are put into the intimate word, as a contribution goes into a fund

parts.note: cosy means snug and intimate
MO is modus operandi, a way of working
a log is a journal or record

explanation.surface: A method and a diary make a personal yet widely applicable piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmology is the study of the universe as a whole, so it is literally relevant to the universe.

clue.text: Develops enough to assume government's keen on containing dispute

indicators.note: the government letters hold the dispute between them

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government, with S from the possessive
a row is a quarrel or dispute
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An administration eager on a quarrel matures into taking on a role.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow into a role or garment is to develop until it fits, so you can take it on.

clue.text: Partly autobiographical figure in work of non-fiction?

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A semi-autobiographical character appears in a factual book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a character in a memoir, but it means a chart or diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a figure, a chart printed to illustrate data, as found in factual books.

clue.text: What could possibly interest foodies ignoring the starter and staring into space?

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped, starter meaning the opening letter, not a first course

parts.note: gastronomy, the art of good eating, would interest food lovers

explanation.surface: A foodie skips the first course and gazes vacantly into the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' fits the food surface, but here it is the first letter; 'staring into space' is not daydreaming but looking at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the scientific study of stars and planets, literally gazing into outer space.

clue.text: Channels transmitting material that's too much for other outlets

definitions.text: Channels transmitting material that's too much for other outlets

parts.words: Channels transmitting material that's too much for other outlets
parts.note: sounds like TV channels for content other media won't take, but means pipes carrying excess water away

explanation.surface: Television stations broadcast content too extreme for mainstream media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channels' and 'outlets' suggest broadcasters and media; they are drains and pipes for surplus water.
explanation.definitionFit: Overflow pipes channel away surplus water that ordinary drains cannot take.

clue.text: Inclusive event is about to include training

indicators.note: the word for about holds the training letters inside it

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
PE is physical education, training for the body

explanation.surface: An event for everyone is about to add a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: An open competition is one any player may enter, so it includes all comers.

clue.text: Study about attention in school

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the school letters

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Pupils learn about paying attention in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is detailed study to discover new facts.

clue.text: Middle of article is replaced by author's sentence

indicators.note: the central letter of the article word is the one taken away
the central letter is swapped out for the author's letters

parts.note: the is the definite article
the author's 'I am' is I'M, the setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer gets punished when the core of their piece is rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is THE, not the word 'article': 'Middle of' names its H, and 'is replaced by' puts IM there.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time.

clue.text: Counterfeit money for bishop in jar

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: to jar is to grate on or annoy
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: Forged cash is swapped for a churchman inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a pot, but it is a verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterfeit something is to copy or imitate it fraudulently.

clue.text: City quietly abandoning affected game

indicators.note: the quiet letter leaves the affected word

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A city gives up quietly playing a pretentious game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is an English university city, home to the university where Hawking worked.

clue.text: Something that's stemmed from bully tipping lager over

parts.note: to cow is to bully or intimidate

indicators.note: tipping the drink up, together with over, turns it around
with tipping it says the lager is turned back to front

parts.note: pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A thug knocks a pint over, with something resulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stemmed from' suggests resulting from; here a thing that's stemmed simply has a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowslip is a wild flower that grows on a stalk, so it has a stem.

clue.text: Rob's recently stolen picture from police station

parts.note: mugs means robs, with the 's as is
hot goods have been recently stolen

explanation.surface: A thief nicks a photo taken at the station.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is the photo the police take of an arrested person.

clue.text: 12 perhaps raised money to help school outside Reading?

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: aid is money given to help

indicators.note: the school word goes round the reading letter

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
R is reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: Funds are raised to help a school outside the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the English town, but it is R, one of the three Rs of basic education.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph, the answer to 12, is one kind of diagram.

clue.text: Issue instructions to lawyer

definitions.meaning: British slang for a barrister or defence lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone gives orders to their legal counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefing is giving instructions, and in British slang a criminal's solicitor or barrister is their brief.

clue.text: Unofficial Labour leader divides support

indicators.note: the first letter splits the support word in two

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: the leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel Labour leader splits the party's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unofficial' looks like it describes the leader, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Black, as in the black economy, means unofficial and not declared to the authorities.

clue.text: Somehow we salvage one that has to work

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: We rescue some poor drudge who is obliged to labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage slave is someone wholly dependent on a job's pay, so they must keep working.

clue.text: Fare from Japan in vessel almost circumnavigating America

indicators.note: the shortened vessel sails round the American letters
almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a ship is a vessel
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Japanese food on board a ship that nearly went round the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price for the voyage, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: A duty borne by nursemaid for religious leader

indicators.note: the nursemaid carries the other pieces inside her, as a child is carried

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid in India
a toll is a charge or duty paid for passage

explanation.surface: A charge is carried by a nanny on behalf of a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite cleric, especially in Iran.

clue.text: Money-lender yields capital with greater confidence

indicators.note: gives up its capital letter, its first, rather than handing over money

parts.note: a usurer lends money at excessive interest

explanation.surface: A loan shark hands over funds, feeling more certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in a lending surface, but it is the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Surer means more certain, which is having greater confidence.

clue.text: Retains retro look capturing product's novelty

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so everything is read in reverse
the look word holds the selling point inside it

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
USP is a unique selling point, what is new about a product

explanation.surface: A vintage style holds on to what makes a product new.
explanation.walkthrough: USP, a unique selling point, is marketing jargon for what sets a product apart; 'retro' reverses the combined letters PUSPEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something up is to maintain or retain it.

clue.text: Herald magnificent achievement?

definitions.meaning: the Herald was a car model made by the British manufacturer ...

explanation.surface: Announce a splendid success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' reads as a verb, to announce, but it is the Triumph Herald, a small British car of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement, and Triumph made the Herald car.
